forces.title: Evolution of travel planning to multi-orbit, iterative journey
forces.description: The travel customer journey has fundamentally shifted from a linear path to a looping, 'orbital' process, increasing touchpoints to 65 in 2026 from 45 in 2018. Inspiration now occurs continuously through everyday entertainment like social media and AI, preceding explicit intent. Booking decisions are less final due to flexible policies and ongoing recommendations, allowing travelers to reconsider and even change booked accommodations, signifying a profound change in consumer engagement with travel planning.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Fragmented travel research experience creates 'restart tax'
forces.description: Travelers navigate numerous channels—search engines, OTAs, social media, AI—for research, but these tools rarely share context, resulting in a 'restart tax'. Handoffs between platforms strip away previously gathered information, forcing travelers to re-enter preferences and re-evaluate options. This friction is a leading cause of negative sentiment and decision fatigue, increasing the risk of travelers abandoning a trip idea for a less complicated alternative. Continuity remains an unsolved industry problem.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Increasing AI adoption in travel inspiration and planning
forces.description: AI is rapidly emerging as a significant source of travel inspiration and planning, with 71% of travelers comfortable using it for ideas today and 86% considering AI bookings in the future. AI can swiftly generate detailed itineraries and alternatives, leveraging a meta-layer of content. Its growing use in initial inspiration sessions underscores its transformative impact on how travelers discover and research trips, indicating a fundamental shift in the technological landscape of the travel sector.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: AI trust gap hinders booking conversions despite speed
forces.description: Despite AI's ability to rapidly generate itineraries, traveler confidence in AI for final booking decisions is not advancing at the same rate. Consumers frequently verify AI-generated information, prices, and availability through trusted sources like reviews, friends, and OTAs. This 'trust gap' means AI's speed doesn't necessarily translate into quicker final decisions, and in some cases, paradoxically increases total research time, as travelers perform additional validation steps before committing to a booking.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Strong consumer preference for experience-led spending
forces.description: Consumers are increasingly prioritizing 'standout experiences' over material goods, with 47% expressing this preference. They demonstrate a willingness to travel and spend more for events deemed 'once-in-a-lifetime'. This mindset, evidenced by significant consumer spending around major live events, fuels sustained demand for travel and leisure experiences, premium offerings, and services that enhance social moments, creating a powerful upside driver for operators focused on unique experiential value propositions.

forces.title: Growing global wellness economy boosts related services
forces.description: The global wellness economy is projected to expand significantly, with an 8% annual growth rate through 2030. This growth is driven by consumers broadening their definition of wellness beyond traditional exercise to encompass holistic well-being. This shift leads to increased spending on diverse wellness categories, including gym memberships, fitness experiences, and a variety of wellness services, creating substantial tailwinds and growth opportunities for the wellness sub-segment within Travel, Tourism & Leisure.
forces.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

forces.title: Heightened competition for sustained consumer attention
forces.description: The expanding scope and complexity of travel planning, fueled by continuous inspiration from social media and AI, means destinations and platforms are competing intensely for sustained consumer attention, not just an initial click. Travelers can easily pivot to different trip ideas if friction arises or a more appealing option emerges. This intensified battle demands constant engagement and re-engagement from travel players, as capturing attention once is insufficient for conversion in this fluid environment.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: User-generated content and influencers drive booking confidence
forces.description: Trust in recommendations from friends/family (65% of travelers) and travel creators/influencers (67%) is a primary driver for inspiration and booking confidence. Authentic user-generated content and genuine customer feedback, even highlighting imperfections, significantly boost conversion by providing relatability and transparency. Operators who cultivate and leverage story-worthy guest experiences, supported by locally fluent and engaging staff, can enhance credibility and effectively drive bookings, particularly for long-haul markets, by tapping into these trusted sources of information.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Discretionary spending pullback amid economic caution
forces.description: Based on US consumer surveys, intentions to pull back spending across most discretionary categories are prevalent due to economic caution, rising prices (52% concern), and cost-of-living worries. This restraint affects all income segments, with lower-income consumers particularly impacted and higher-income consumers cutting 'nice to haves.' This generalized reduction in discretionary spending poses a significant headwind for the Travel, Tourism & Leisure sector, which relies heavily on consumer optionality and disposable income.
forces.source_title: An update on US consumer sentiment: Holiday budgeting begins

forces.title: Declining booking commitment and increased cancellations
forces.description: Booking confirmation no longer signifies a final decision, with half of travelers changing booked accommodations post-booking after discovering more attractive options. Flexible change and cancellation policies, coupled with continuous price monitoring and an endless stream of new recommendations, contribute to this booking fluidity. This creates a significant key risk for operators in terms of revenue predictability and inventory management, necessitating active post-booking engagement to retain customers and mitigate potential churn.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Sticky UK inflation and elevated borrowing costs
forces.description: The UK is experiencing persistent inflation, with a headline forecast of +2.9% in 2026, driven by ongoing wage growth and anticipated energy price hikes. Concurrently, borrowing costs are expected to remain elevated, with the Bank Rate projected at 4.00% through September 2027. This combination of sticky inflation and higher financing expenses constrains household disposable incomes, acting as a significant cyclical headwind that impacts consumer spending on discretionary categories like travel and leisure.
forces.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

forces.title: Strategic investment in technology and innovation for experiences
forces.description: UK Hospitality & Leisure businesses are proactively investing in technology and innovation to enhance customer experiences, build loyalty, and drive long-term value. This strategic focus enables adaptation to evolving customer expectations and operational pressures. By leveraging new technologies, operators can create more memorable and personalized offerings, differentiate themselves in a competitive market, and unlock growth opportunities despite tightening margins and economic uncertainty, thereby serving as a significant upside driver for the sector's future.
forces.source_title: Hospitality and Leisure: Serving up success

forces.title: Consumer preference for curated travel options
forces.description: Travelers are increasingly overwhelmed by the sheer volume of choices and information, leading to anxiety in booking decisions. A significant majority (63%) express a preference for a curated set of ten recommended options over a full catalog or a single AI-generated plan. This indicates a structural shift in consumer demand towards credible, short-listed options with clear reasoning, presenting a strategic opportunity for platforms and operators that can effectively implement curation while maintaining consumer control and choice.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Cross-session continuity in travel planning enhances engagement
forces.description: Improving customer journey continuity by retaining saved content, budgets, rejected options, and preferences across devices and sessions is a critical upside driver. Travelers currently experience a 'restart tax' due to fragmented context. Platforms that make returning to a planning session seamless and easier than starting over, leveraging structured context and conversational AI for conflict resolution, will gain a significant competitive advantage. This enhances customer engagement, reduces friction, and ultimately drives higher conversion rates and retention.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Operational strain from concentrated demand spikes
forces.description: Major live events, while driving significant revenue, create concentrated short-term demand spikes across hospitality, leisure, and retail, as exemplified by the Harry Styles concert. These surges pose a key operational risk if businesses are not adequately prepared. Implications for staffing, stock management, pricing strategies, and cash flow—including managing working capital and supplier payments—must be proactively addressed to fully capitalize on these opportunities and avoid disruptions, ensuring that demand translates efficiently into successful operations.

forces.title: Broadening consumer definition of holistic wellness
forces.description: Consumers are increasingly adopting a holistic view of wellness, extending beyond traditional exercise to encompass overall well-being. This expanded definition includes diverse motivations such as improving cardiovascular health, managing weight, supporting longevity, and enhancing mental health, varying across demographics. This structural shift in consumer perception drives investment across a broader spectrum of wellness categories and services, creating new opportunities for the wellness sub-segment within Travel, Tourism & Leisure to cater to these evolving, comprehensive health objectives.
forces.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

viewpoints.title: Travel players face competitive fragmentation but can win with continuity
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's Travel Practice identifies a dramatically evolved customer journey, now an 'orbit' with 65 touchpoints, up from 45 in 2018. This fragmented, non-linear path creates intense competition and a higher risk of losing travelers. However, underlying traveler needs for enjoyable and affordable experiences remain constant. Success lies in creating continuity and confidence across touchpoints, smoothing friction, and actively maintaining engagement from inspiration through post-booking. Operators must strategically earn and sustain attention rather than relying on single conversion points.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Global wellness economy growth creates tailwinds for related services
viewpoints.description: BCG's research indicates that the global wellness economy is poised for robust growth, forecast to expand approximately 8% annually through 2030, outperforming many discretionary categories. This growth is driven by consumers expanding their definition of fitness to holistic wellbeing, leading to increased spending on adjacent wellness categories such as gym memberships, fitness experiences, and wellness services. This trend provides powerful tailwinds for the wellness sub-segment within Travel, Tourism & Leisure, offering significant opportunities for service providers.
viewpoints.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

viewpoints.title: UK H&L leaders optimistic about major event-driven demand
viewpoints.description: Sixty percent of UK hospitality and leisure (H&L) industry leaders express optimism, anticipating that the summer calendar of major sporting and cultural events will significantly bolster trading conditions. This confidence is underpinned by the substantial consumer spending generated by large-scale live events, such as the Harry Styles concert, which funnels demand into associated travel, accommodation, food, drink, merchandise, and leisure activities, creating valuable short-term spikes for businesses in surrounding areas.

viewpoints.title: UK Hospitality & Leisure demonstrates resilience despite mounting pressures
viewpoints.description: Rich Robinson, Head of Hospitality and Leisure at Barclays Corporate Banking, observes the UK hospitality and leisure industry's remarkable resilience and adaptability. Despite contending with tightening margins, selective consumer spending, economic/political uncertainty, and evolving customer expectations, 88% of H&L businesses report confidence in their prospects for the next year. This confidence stems from strategic investments in technology and innovation, which are aimed at creating memorable customer experiences to build loyalty and unlock long-term value in a dynamic market.
viewpoints.source_title: Hospitality and Leisure: Serving up success

demand_drivers.description: Consumers are broadening their view of fitness to overall wellbeing, increasing spending in related categories like gym memberships, fitness experiences, and wellness services.
Wellness spending accelerates during pivotal life moments such as youth sports, weight-loss journeys, and setting new fitness goals.

market_sizing.methodology: The global wellness economy is projected to expand significantly, driven by consumers increasing and diversifying their spending on wellness-related categories. This includes a growing allocation towards services such as gym memberships, various fitness experiences, and broader wellness services, reflecting an expanded definition of holistic well-being beyond just physical exercise.
market_sizing.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

demand_drivers.description: Large-scale sporting, musical, and cultural events attract significant consumer spending on associated travel, accommodation, and leisure activities, driving short-term demand spikes.
Consumers prioritize spending on standout experiences, often willing to travel or spend more for 'once-in-a-lifetime' events over material goods.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated total consumer spending linked to Harry Styles' 12-date Wembley Stadium concert in summer 2026. This figure encompasses expenditure on tickets, travel, accommodation, food and drink, merchandise, and broader leisure activities. The average spend per attendee for these events was calculated at £981, based on real transaction data and consumer research.
